newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: SOCCER-SLAVIA PRAGUE TAKES FIRST-EVER CZECH CUP.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SLAVIA PRAGUE TAKES FIRST-EVER CZECH CUP.

text.p: Slavia Prague earned itself a place in European soccer competition next season, beating upstart second division Dukla Prague 1-0 in extra time on Sunday to take the Czech-Moravian Cup.

Slavia, which salvaged some pride with the win after losing the first division title to crosstown rivals Sparta Prague earlier this week, used its trademark smothering defense to foil Dukla as it pressed to end the game in regulation time.
Both teams tried to attack from the start of extra-time, looking for the sudden death golden goal that would decide the match.
Neither had to wait long as striker Karel Rada found the back of the goal 10 minutes into extra-time to give Slavia its first-ever national cup.
"It was excellent football," said Slavia coach Frantisek Cipro. "We had a lot of luck. We can thank (goalkeeper Jan) Stejskal for it by keeping the opposition off of the scoreboard."

Despite the loss, Dukla, the former army team under communism which had fallen on hard times in recent years, can take solace in the fact that earlier this week it regained a spot in first division competition after winning the second league title.
